usages.explain:
It is used when the speaker wants to base their judgment on the content of the story just mentioned, to express their judgment on that matter.
Following this, there are expressions that convey the speaker's judgment or those that give permission, advice, or suggestions. People also say「ということなら」.

examples.content: したくないと言うのなら、してもらわなくてもいい。
examples.transcription: したくないというのなら、してもらわなくてもいい。
examples.mean: If you say you don't want to do it, you don't have to do it.

examples.content: 健康が大切だと言うのなら、タバコを止めなければならない。
examples.transcription: けんこうがたいせつだというのなら、たばこをとめなければならない。
examples.mean: If your health is important to you, you must stop smoking.

title: というのなら => If say that
